agree.reason: The nurse's own visit log and the neighbouring district's results make a credible case, but a parent who works an 8 a.m. shift gets only a promise of a future plan, so a resistant reader may not be won over.

honest.reason: The piece honestly turns down the brief's request to promise a higher graduation rate, but it makes two small overreaches: "It's also why" ties the AAP recommendation to the local survey, and "every high school student can actually use" first period overstates.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out several useful figures (the 369 combined total, "nearly three in four," "one in six"), but it never puts the $180,000 into a per-student or per-day cost, which would have made it look smaller.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is described fairly as more of the same first-period problems, and the brief has no trend data the piece leaves out.

qualification.reason: The hedges ("won't claim a bell schedule alone will change that number," a childcare plan "before the change takes effect") give no date, number or consequence that a reader could check.

objections.reason: It takes on cost, athletics and parent drop-off directly, but it never answers the practices-after-dark point and it pushes the working-parent gap off to a later district plan.

fit.reason: This is a properly structured op-ed with a headline and byline, and at about 625 words it is under the 650-word limit.
